title: Finite reduction of supported Kummer products and the diagonal orientation chain
statement:
Fix the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A=A_{E,n}$, $B=A_{E,m}$, $1\le m\le n$. All schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Work in the ordinary small pro-etale bounded constructible finite-Tor categories and put $Q_T=(-)\otimes_A^LB$. Use the specified Tate twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], actual coefficient comparisons [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons], and their shifted-line and zero-section exceptional versions [def-pur-finite-affine-orientation-comparison].

For a zero section $s:S\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_S$, let $c_{s(S),R}:s_*R_S\to R_{\mathbf A^1_S}(1)[2]$, $R=A,B$, be the supported Cartier-Kummer map [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], and $o_{s,R}:R_S\to Rs_R^!R_{\mathbf A^1_S}(1)[2]$ its exceptional adjunct, the orientation of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. Under the specified comparisons,
$$Q_{\mathbf A^1_S}(c_{s(S),A})=c_{s(S),B},\qquad Q_S(o_{s,A})=o_{s,B}.$$
For every $r\ge0$ and zero section $z:S\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^r_S$, the same reduction identity holds for the ordered $r$-fold supported product giving $\mathrm{th}_{r,R}:R_S\to Rz_R^!R_{\mathbf A^r_S}(r)[2r]$ of [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity]; for $r=0$ this is the unit.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$. Put $W=X\times_YX$, with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow W$. Its normal bundle $N=N_{\Delta/W}\cong T_{X/Y}$ has rank $d$ [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion, def-pur-normal-bundle]; write $\pi:N\to X$ and $z:X\to N$. Set $\omega_{f,R}=Rf_R^!R_Y$, $C_R(g,t)=Lt^*Rg_R^!R_{\mathrm{base}(g)}$ [def-pur-section-invariant]. Let $a_R:\omega_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_R(p_1,\Delta)$ be the inverse diagonal base-change identification [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], $\delta_R:C_R(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_R(\pi,z)$ the normalized DNC comparison [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], and $v_R:C_R(\pi,z)\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X(d)[2d]$ the zero-section restriction of the integration-normalized vector-bundle comparison [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. The diagonal orientation is the specified map
$$\alpha_{f,R}=v_R\delta_Ra_R:\omega_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X(d)[2d]$$
of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object], with its actual local assembly as in [lem-pur-diagonal-dnc-chart-normalization]. Denote the coefficient comparisons on $\omega_f,C(p_1,\Delta),C(\pi,z),R_X(d)[2d]$ respectively by $q_\omega,q_C,q_N,q_L$. Then
$$q_CQ_X(a_A)=a_Bq_\omega,\qquad q_NQ_X(\delta_A)=\delta_Bq_C,\qquad q_LQ_X(v_A)=v_Bq_N.$$
Consequently $q_LQ_X(\alpha_{f,A})=\alpha_{f,B}q_\omega$. All identities concern these normalized maps, including arbitrary ramification, identity reductions and relative dimension zero.

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] to the effective Cartier divisor $s(S)$: the coordinate $t$ is a nonzerodivisor even when $S$ is nonreduced. Its coefficient-compatibility clause is the supported Ext equation with the actual scalar-extension units of [def-amb-proetale-supported-coefficient-reduction]. Those units send supported constants by $a\mapsto\bar a$ and root-limit tensors by $x\otimes a\mapsto x\otimes\bar a$. By their stated universal property, the Ext equation is exactly equality of the two $B$-linear derived adjuncts, namely $Q(c_{s(S),A})=c_{s(S),B}$ under the prescribed source and target comparisons. These are the coefficient-unit and shifted-line comparisons of [def-pur-finite-affine-orientation-comparison], not chosen trivializations. The Cartier theorem allows every positive uniformizer level and arbitrary ramification.

source.place: Step 4, affine orientations; Step 3, reduction of the supported Kummer boundary

proof.text: For $s$, the last clause of [lem-pur-finite-adjoint-mate-compatibility] identifies the reduction of the exceptional transpose of a compact-support arrow with the transpose of its reduction. Apply it to $s_*A_S\to A_{\mathbf A^1_S}(1)[2]$ from Step 1. The resulting transpose is $o_{s,B}$, since [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] and [def-pur-finite-affine-orientation-comparison] identify the affine orientation with this supported boundary's adjunct. Thus $Q_S(o_{s,A})=o_{s,B}$, including the coefficient-unit input comparison. The zero section is closed and all the schemes are separated finite type, so this is within the cited adjunction domain.

source.place: Step 4, Kummer orientation and exceptional adjunction

proof.text: Here is the scalar calculation for the supported product. In [def-pur-supported-cup] its source comparison is multiplication $\theta_R:i_*R_Z\otimes_R^Lj_*R_W\simeq h_*R_{Z\times_TW}$, and its shift comparison on $P[a]^u\otimes Q[b]^v$ is multiplication by $(-1)^{bu}$. The same statement identifies each closed supported constant with a flat quotient of the constant coefficient sheaf. Consequently its scalar extension is the corresponding $B$-supported constant. On local sections both scalar/multiplication composites send $(x\otimes y)\otimes b$ to $\bar x\bar yb$; this proves the square for $\theta$, and hence for its inverse. Scalar change preserves the displayed sign. The finite-reduction tensor/unit coherence of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] identifies the intervening tensor maps. The last map in [def-pur-supported-class-operations] is ordered Tate multiplication; its scalar square sends every root tensor with coefficient $a$ to that same root tensor with coefficient $\bar a$, by the specified line and tensor-power comparisons [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons, def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Thus reduction of the explicitly defined cup composite is the cup composite of the reductions.

source.place: Step 3, supported products and their coefficient maps

proof.text: Induct on the number $r$ of ordered coordinate divisors in $\mathbf A^r_S$. The empty product is the coefficient unit, whose reduction is the unit by [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons]. For the successor product, regard the first $j$ factors and the $(j+1)$st factor as supported arrows on this same affine space. Each factor reduces by the Cartier theorem used in Step 1; Step 3 gives reduction of their cup product. This proves by induction equality of the ordered $r$-fold supported maps. The supports intersect in the scheme-theoretic zero section, since the sum of their coordinate ideals is $(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$. By [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity] this is the supported product defining $\mathrm{th}_{r,R}$ after exceptional transposition. The transpose clause of [lem-pur-finite-adjoint-mate-compatibility] therefore gives the claimed reduction identity for $\mathrm{th}_r$. This argument also covers $r=0$ without a divisor or a Kummer class.

source.place: Steps 3-4, ordered products and the affine zero-section orientations

proof.text: Apply the separately stated inverse-alpha coefficient square [lem-pur-finite-diagonal-base-change-reduction] to the actual normalized base-change factor. This is the first conjunct of the diagonal theorem.

source.place: Step 3, coefficient compatibility of the diagonal base-change constituent

proof.text: The separate theorem [lem-pur-finite-diagonal-dnc-reduction] records the coefficient squares for centred source and normal coordinates and the resulting normalized DNC equality. Its proof compares the exceptional mates and the coefficient-independent normal frame in every chart.

source.place: Step 3, actual etale coordinates for the normalized DNC comparison

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-finite-diagonal-dnc-reduction] to obtain the second conjunct, the delta coefficient square. Coordinate-normalized uniqueness and locality are contained in that genuinely separate DNC step.

source.place: Step 3, normalization and uniqueness of the DNC gluing

proof.text: Obtain the generator-normalized coefficient-line comparison e and the vector-factor square from [lem-pur-finite-diagonal-vector-reduction]. This gives the third conjunct and fixes the same e that will be used for the composite square.

source.place: Steps 3-4, integration-normalized vector-bundle constituent and its actual finite coefficient map

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-finite-diagonal-orientation-assembly] at each coefficient stage to write the actual orientation as inverse alpha, then delta, then the vector factor. A functor maps this composite to the composite of the images. Compose the three squares furnished by [lem-pur-finite-diagonal-base-change-reduction], [lem-pur-finite-diagonal-dnc-reduction] and [lem-pur-finite-diagonal-vector-reduction]; associativity yields the required last equality. This is a direct Lean calculation. Assembly is coefficient-independent and applies globally, including empty schemes and dimension zero. All comparisons remain the specified maps, including identity reductions.

Step 2 uses the last (transpose) clause of mate-compatibility for the closed zero section.
